summary.headline: TCI Express Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR 312 crore, with PAT up 6% to INR 22.4 crore and volumes up 7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes.
summary.overview: Income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 312 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR 37 crore, with margin at 11.7% versus 11.5%. PAT rose 6% to INR 22.4 crore (7.1% margin). Management said the fuel price hike taken in mid-May was only partly reflected in Q1 (June only), so benefits should show from Q2. The company stated it is debt-free with net cash of about INR 118 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~6% YoY from INR 21 crore; margin 7.1%

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; grew 9% YoY on existing customers, new accounts and industrial growth. Management targets accelerating to double-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY per opening remarks (CEO-level figure); later cited ~28% on enterprise account wins and airline partnerships.

segments.name: International Express
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY on new customers, win-backs and expanded global carrier partnerships.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: Grew 63% YoY, the fastest-growing vertical, but only ~2-2.5% of revenue; target small-merchant, D2C and e-commerce B2B segments at 16-18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Rail Express / C2C Express
segments.commentary: Rail added operational branches; C2C added clients, regional branch coverage and a larger dedicated vehicle fleet. No growth figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 11-12%, with net price realisation of about 3%, implying 13-15% overall revenue growth.
EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps targeted for FY27; margin benefit from fuel pass-through expected from Q2.
Multimodal share of revenue targeted at 17-18% to 19% in FY27 and 22-25% by 2030.
FY27 capex guided at INR 125-140 crore; management said it expects to cross INR 125 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.
Kolkata hub automation expected by March 2027 or June 2027 at latest; Ahmedabad around mid-2027, taking automated hubs to four by 2027.
capex_capacity: Two hubs automated so far: Tajnagar (North India) and Chakan (Pune); Kolkata and Ahmedabad under construction.
Ongoing construction at four sites: Ahmedabad, Kolkata, corporate office and Lucknow.
Management said it is close to finalising a land purchase in one of Mumbai, Chennai or Bangalore.
Regional branch expansion ongoing across Surface, Air, Rail and C2C; e-commerce regional branches being opened and bikers hired for sub-5 kg deliveries.
demand_pricing: Volume grew ~7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes, but management said price hikes were held back until fuel increased in mid-May; diesel and annual hikes together gave a 'handsome' increase, with ~90%+ of customers passed through in June.
Analyst noted peers are taking 3-5% price hikes; management did not give a specific Q1 price-hike percentage.
SME to B2B mix returned to 50:50 in Q1 from 48:52 in FY26.
Management cited pipeline visibility, manufacturing demand and SME recovery; growth expected from both existing customers and new industries.
Analyst raised competitive pricing in certain segments and elevated operating costs industry-wide; management said its service quality and tech investment keep it ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q1 volumes and price hikes versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 2.5 lakh tonnes, up ~7.5%. Management said fuel-linked pass-through came in mid-May, with the full price increase reflected mainly in June; the company deferred hikes ahead of expected fuel increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for expanding e-commerce given lower margins historically?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is ~2-2.5% of revenue. Management said D2C margins are 16-18% and it is targeting small merchants, D2C and e-commerce B2B, with regional teams and branches to support Surface.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to drive consistent double-digit EBITDA growth and volume acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it strengthened vertical-wise regional teams and built regional structures across Air, International, Rail and C2C. Air grew ~28% on new customers, and a clear pipeline supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume, pricing and PAT targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 11-12%, net price hikes of about 3%, total growth of 13-15%, and PAT growth of 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of hub automation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Two hubs are automated (Tajnagar, Chakan); Kolkata is expected by March or June 2027 and Ahmedabad around mid-2027. FY27 capex is INR 125-140 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins improve in Q2 as fuel pass-through takes full effect, and what is the multimodal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fuel increase was passed on to 90%+ of customers in June, so margins should improve from Q2. Multimodal share is about 17-18% now, targeted at 17-19% this year and 22-25% by 2030.

risks_watch: Realisation: management said price hikes were deferred and partly reflected only in June, so Q2 pricing and margin uplift need to be verified.
Net price hike guidance of ~3% is below the 3-5% peers were said to be taking; the analyst questioned this.
E-commerce last-mile economics: management cited 16-18% EBITDA margin, but the analyst questioned profitability in last-mile delivery.
Capex of INR 125-140 crore against INR 20 crore spent so far; land purchase timing is uncertain.
Management's 11-12% volume and 20-25% PAT growth guidance is ambitious against 7.5% volume growth and 6% PAT growth in Q1.
Domestic Air growth figure inconsistency: 29% in prepared remarks versus ~28% in Q&A.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, pipeline and margin recovery, but vague on specifics such as the Q1 price-hike percentage and the e-commerce economics. Answers were often loosely structured and repetitive.
key_quotes: We are very much clear about volume growth in the range of 11% to 12% volume growth and price hikes net of about around 3%.
So this year capex is around INR125 crores to INR140 crores.
So yes, in quarter ahead you will see the very good number increase in that margin level.
The star of the quarter was our E-commerce Express business, which surged 63% year-on-year to become our fastest -growing service vertical by a wide margin
